advisory.finding: A DET-passing agentic run's INDETERMINATE is still written to the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar. It becomes the newest sidecar, so a later pipeline run's BLOCK verdict reuse finds a non-BLOCK latest review and pays for a full LLM re-review, even though the plan and the code did not change.
scenarios: A ticket has a stored BLOCK. Someone runs review_plan(engine='agentic') once, or with plan_review_engine='agentic' configured, then switches back to pipeline. The next pipeline review_plan runs the full billable multi-pass review instead of reusing the BLOCK.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _run_plan_review, skip sidecar.emit (sidecar_emitted=False) when engine != 'pipeline' and the verdict degraded, the same way the cancelled-stale verdict skips the sidecar. Add a test: review BLOCK under pipeline, run agentic, then confirm pipeline still returns coverage.verdict_reuse=True with zero calls.

advisory.finding: The deliberate 'agentic engine not available' outcome reaches the generic LLM-outage path. It is stamped coverage.llm_unavailable=True and logged as an LLM degrade, so consumers cannot tell a configuration choice from a provider outage. The post-dispatch tail gate also relies on that same mislabeled flag.
scenarios: An operator sets plan_review_engine='agentic'. Every DET-passing review then shows up as an LLM outage in sidecars, logs and review-bot coverage reasons, and the engine name appears only inside the llm_error string.

evidence: Added gate in _run_plan_review: `if engine == "pipeline" or not verdict.get("coverage", {}).get("llm_unavailable"):` then `_apply_review_floors(...)`

tests/unit/test_plan_review_engine_switch.py:145: `assert runner.calls == calls_before  # zero LLM calls` is the only check on the tail under agentic, and the tail makes no calls in these fixtures anyway
No test spies on `_apply_review_floors` (or a floor entry point) and asserts it is not called under agentic DET-pass but is called under the agentic floor-passthrough case
advisory.finding: The new rule that skips the post-dispatch tail (`if engine == "pipeline" or not verdict.get("coverage", {}).get("llm_unavailable")`) has no regression coverage. Every agentic test checks 'zero LLM calls' through `runner.calls == calls_before`, but in each tested setup the tail would make no call anyway. The rising floor returns early unless a remediation re-review is in progress. The completion floor returns early unless the ticket has children and `completion_floor_active` is on. The degraded verdict has no advisory findings and fewer than two blocking ones. So if the `engine == "pipeline" or ...` guard were deleted, every test would still pass.
scenarios: A later refactor drops the engine condition from the tail gate. An agentic run on a remediation re-review, or on a container ticket with completion_floor_active, then makes pipeline floor or xcheck LLM sub-calls, which breaks ADR 0123's 'an agentic run makes no pipeline LLM call'. No test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch `rebar.llm.plan_review._apply_review_floors` with a recording spy. Assert it is not called by `review_plan(tid, engine="agentic")` on `_PASSING_DESC`. Assert it is called for `_FLOOR_BLOCKED_DESC` under both engines and for a DET-passing pipeline review.
